title: Parameter normalization and repair hints: permissive parsing, user-facing diagnostics
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Define a permissive JSON-schema declaration format and runtime normalization rules for function/tool parameters. Deliver clear diagnostic messages and repair hints that enable calling clients (SDKs and UI) to surface actionable fixes for common user errors and compatibility issues.
rationale: Current parameter validation is strict and returns opaque errors that cause retries and poor developer UX. We need a middle ground: a canonical schema plus a permissive parsing layer that can auto-repair or surface deterministic hints so downstream callers can recover without developer support tickets.
tradeoffs: Permissive parsing increases runtime complexity and risk of silent misinterpretation if repair heuristics are too aggressive
Stricter validation reduces ambiguity but causes more friction for integrators and increases support load
Providing rich repair hints increases payload size and requires careful i18n and privacy review in the future
design_goals: Define a compact declaration format compatible with existing function-call schemas
Support best-effort normalization for common problems (trailing commas, unquoted keys in hand-authored JSON, numeric strings, date formats)
Produce deterministic error codes and short, human-readable repair hints for SDKs and Console UI
Allow opt-in strict mode per-route or per-customer for compliance-sensitive customers
implementation_plan: Design schema extension: add optional 'normalizationHints' and 'deprecatedAliases' fields to function declarations
Implement permissive parser in runtime core with a pluggable repair pipeline (heuristics are rules-driven)
Expose a consolidated diagnostic object: {error_code, message, hint, repaired_value?, confidence}
Update JS and Python SDKs to surface repair hints and offer an opt-in auto-repair flag
Add console level telemetry to track repairs and false-positives for tuning heuristics
acceptance_criteria: Runtime accepts weakly-formatted but recoverable inputs and returns standardized diagnostics for all repairs
SDKs can toggle auto-repair and present the same hint text shown in runtime diagnostics
No change in behavior for strict-mode routes; strict mode rejects inputs using existing error codes
Telemetry exposes per-rule precision/recall so heuristics can be incrementally tuned
Security review signoff confirming no sensitive information is inferred or leaked by repair hints
test_plan: Unit tests for each normalization rule with golden inputs and expected repaired outputs
Fuzzing harness that feeds malformed JSONs and asserts deterministic diagnostic codes
Integration tests: SDK roundtrip with auto-repair enabled and disabled
Canary rollout to 5% of internal traffic with monitoring dashboard for repair rate and customer-facing errors
progress_updates: 2025-02-13: Kickoff meeting with runtime, SDK, and docs. Agreed on initial heuristic list.
2025-02-20: Prototype parser implemented (trim/strip comments, allow single quotes, coerce numeric-strings). Initial internal tests pass.
2025-02-27: Design review with PM and Security. Security requested explicit opt-out annotation for auto-repair on PII-bearing parameters.
2025-03-03: SDK change events filed (JS-SDK #421, Py-SDK #198). Working on diagnostic schema consensus.
2025-03-04: Began writing telemetry dashboard for repair rule accuracy (console-telemetry-#59).
review_feedback: PM (Miguel Torres): Prefer short, copyable repair hints (<=140 chars) to simplify UI rendering and copy-paste into docs
Design (Hannah Liu): Repair hint UI should show original and repaired value with an undo affordance
Security (Dmitry Ivanov): Explicit opt-out required for auto-repair for any parameter where 'sensitive': true is set
Runtime (Leah Patel): We should implement a confidence score to prevent cascading repairs in multi-rule scenarios
notes: Edge case: array positional repairs (e.g. single-item where schema expects object) require explicit rule to avoid data loss
We will start with a small set of high-confidence repairs and expand via telemetry signals
Plan to publish a short RFC to external integrators explaining backward-compatible opt-in behavior
